editorial: Memory, a psychological thriller, feels like every frame is a chess move, heightening the stakes from the first breathless beat. The assassin’s fractured memory turns each confrontation into a fragile puzzle that keeps you guessing who you can trust. Joaquin Phoenix carries every tense moment with only body language, letting silence do the narrating. The film’s most striking element is its clever manipulation of flashback loops that feel natural rather than gimmicky. Though the middle act stretches a bit, the tension rebuilds to keep you hooked right to the close.
targetAudience: Ideal for fans of psychological thrillers who enjoy non-linear storytelling.
